A parallel sum reduces the encoded exponentials with derived finite-range and
rounding bounds. A two-instruction scalar sequence normalizes each numerator
using the actual stored sum through an explicit register interface. The total
exponential and sum error must be at most one half to derive safe normalization.
The register interface alone does not implement memory operations between stages.
A complete reference forward pipeline now connects the parallel maximum and sum
through sequential fetched exponential and normalization passes in one arena.
It proves execution existence from original bounded finite scores and stored-output
accuracy against TorchLean under the explicit total-error guard. Phase boundaries
are model-level waiting and initialization, not a CUDA runtime implementation.
A fully parallel or fused forward kernel, masking, arbitrary row sizes and a
backward implementation remain separate work.

from.quote:
This component sums the encoded exponential values of a nonempty softmax row
and normalizes one value by that computed sum. The sum has a fixed balanced
binary tree: neighboring pairs are added, then neighboring pair results, until
one value remains. Every addition rounds to the nearest binary32 value, choosing
the even final bit on a tie. The supported row length is a power of two, at most
1024. Each stored input is finite and has absolute value at most two. These are
conditions on the supplied words, not assumptions about successful intermediate
arithmetic. Small negative approximate exponential values are allowed; positivity
must not be inferred from the ideal exponential alone. The existing shifted
exponential sequence supplies the magnitude bound of two from its actual
nonpositive base-two argument and the exponential instruction error contract.

from.quote:
For n inputs, global storage contains n inputs, n positive-one weights, a
positive-zero bias and an output word: 2*n+2 words. Shared storage contains
(depth+1)*n words, where n=2^depth. One cooperating thread array, whose threads
share memory and wait at group barriers, processes the row. Unused initial
registers and shared contents may be arbitrary. Every completed admitted
execution has the stated numerical result and preserves the global input and
constant regions. A separate finite schedule constructs a completed admitted
execution with safe accesses. Neither claim establishes GPU execution, launch
compatibility, scheduler fairness or performance.

theorem completed (d : Nat) (bound : Bounds d) (input : Fin (width d) → Word)
    (shared : List Word) (seeds : Fin (shape d).threads → Scalar.State)
    {events : List (Event (shape d).threads)} {final : State (shape d).threads}
    (run : Runs (config d bound) (program d) (initial d input shared seeds) events final)
    (halted : ∀ t, (final.lanes t).halted=true)
    (source co) (valid : Dense.Admitted (shape d) (denseBounds d bound)
      (global d input) shared seeds run source co) :
    (∃ value, final.global[outputIndex d]?=some value ∧ Output d input value) ∧
    (∀ j : Fin (width d), final.global[j.val]?=some (input j)) ∧
    (∀ i, i<outputIndex d → final.global[i]?=(global d input)[i]?) ∧
    final.global.length=(global d input).length ∧ final.shared.length=shared.length ∧
    (∀ event ∈ events, AccessSafe (initial d input shared seeds) event)

    (shared : List Word) (seeds : Fin (shape d).threads → Scalar.State)

from.quote:
The numerical proof derives finite intermediate sums from the input magnitude
and tree depth. It bounds the error against the exact sum of the actual encoded
input values, keeping it separate from each exponential's error against its
ideal real value. A conservative uniform allowance of 2^-13 per tree addition
covers this bounded domain, giving a sum error at most (n-1)*2^-13. The exact
multiplications by one and final addition of zero introduce no real-value error.
A sharper allowance can replace this bound without changing the arithmetic order.

theorem accuracy (input : Nat → Word) (values : Nat → ℝ) (k offset : Nat) (out : Word)
    (depth : k≤10)
    (finite : ∀j, j<2^k → finiteReal (input (offset+j))=some (values (offset+j)))
    (small : ∀j, j<2^k → |values (offset+j)|≤2)
    (allowed : Reduction.Eval (Reduction.balanced k offset (fun j => (0x3f800000,input j))) out) :
    finiteReal out=some (rounded values k offset) ∧
    |rounded values k offset|≤(2:ℝ)^(k+1) ∧
    |rounded values k offset-ideal values k offset|≤budget k

Let delta_i bound each exponential error and let sigma be the proved summation
allowance. If sigma+sum_i delta_i is at most one half, the stable softmax's ideal
denominator lower bound of one implies that the computed denominator is at
least one half. This guard is explicit; it is not an assumption that the
reciprocal or final result already exists. It also explains which upstream
accuracy information a complete softmax proof must supply.

theorem denominator_lower (exact approximate delta : Fin n→ℝ) (S sigma : ℝ)
    (exponential : ∀ i, |approximate i-exact i|≤delta i)
    (summation : |S-∑i,approximate i|≤sigma) (lower : 1≤∑i,exact i)
    (small : denominatorBudget delta sigma≤1/2) : 1/2≤S

from.quote:
Normalization uses rcp.rn.f32 followed by mul.rn.f32. The reciprocal rounds one
divided by the actual computed denominator; multiplication then uses that
rounded reciprocal and the actual numerator word. The scratch destination must
differ from the numerator register, since the numerator remains live for the
second instruction. It may coincide with the denominator register. From a
finite denominator at least one half and a finite numerator of magnitude at
most two, the proof derives finite reciprocal and product values, their separate
rounding errors, fetched execution existence and preservation of unrelated state.
This is a scalar instruction sequence, not a proof of parallel normalization
stores or of a combined softmax launch.

passage.quote:
theorem correct (target : Ptx.Target) (s t : Scalar.State)
    (numerator denominator destination : Nat) (u S : ℝ)
    (start : s.pc = 0) (scratch : destination ≠ numerator)
    (input : Ptx.Binary32.finiteReal (s.regs numerator) = some u)
    (sum : Ptx.Binary32.finiteReal (s.regs denominator) = some S)
    (small : |u| ≤ 2) (lower : 1/2 ≤ S)
    (run : Run target (program numerator denominator destination) s t) :
    Ptx.Binary32.finiteReal (t.regs destination) = some (round32 (u*round32 (1/S))) ∧
    |round32 (1/S)-1/S| ≤ eps32 (1/S) ∧
    |round32 (u*round32 (1/S))-u*round32 (1/S)| ≤ eps32 (u*round32 (1/S)) ∧
    |round32 (u*round32 (1/S))| ≤ 4

theorem completed_coordinate_accuracy (d : Nat) (bound : Sum.Bounds d)
    (input : Fin (Sum.width d) → Word) (values exact delta : Fin (Sum.width d) → ℝ)
    (finite : ∀i, finiteReal (input i)=some (values i)) (small : ∀i, |values i|≤2)
    (nonneg : ∀i, 0≤exact i) (upper : ∀i, exact i≤1) (lower : 1≤∑i,exact i)
    (exponential : ∀i, |values i-exact i|≤delta i)
    (budget : denominatorBudget delta (SumTree.budget d)≤1/2)
    (shared : List Word) (seeds : Fin (Sum.shape d).threads → Scalar.State)
    {events : List (Event (Sum.shape d).threads)} {sumFinal : State (Sum.shape d).threads}
    (sumRun : Runs (Sum.config d bound) (Sum.program d) (Sum.initial d input shared seeds) events sumFinal)
    (halted : ∀t, (sumFinal.lanes t).halted=true)
    (source co) (valid : Dense.Admitted (Sum.shape d) (Sum.denseBounds d bound)
      (Sum.global d input) shared seeds sumRun source co)
    (target : Ptx.Target) (normalized : Fin (Sum.width d) → Scalar.State)
    (runs : ∀i, Scalar.Normalize.Run target program
      (entry (input i) sumFinal.global[Sum.outputIndex d]!) (normalized i))
    (i : Fin (Sum.width d)) :
    ∃ y, finiteReal ((normalized i).regs 2)=some y ∧
      |y-exact i/(∑j,exact j)|≤coordinateBudget (delta i)
        (denominatorBudget delta (SumTree.budget d))
        (TorchLean.Floats.eps32 (1/Sum.rounded d values))
        (TorchLean.Floats.eps32 (values i*TorchLean.Floats.round32 (1/Sum.rounded d values)))

The reduction kernel also offers an affine-only output option that leaves signed
results intact. The ReLU forward variant retains its existing computation. This
shared implementation avoids duplicating the reduction and synchronization
proofs for the transposed matrix-vector product. A copy kernel constructs the
transposed operand buffer from the actual stored
gated sensitivities and original weights. Each copied word comes from a fetched
load and store. Appending freshly allocated zero words and selecting the copied
buffer as the next kernel's allocation are explicit operations of the host model.
They perform no gradient arithmetic and do not constitute a CUDA allocation,
transfer, synchronization or pointer-ABI implementation.

passage.quote:
The reciprocal of a number x is one divided by x. This instruction responsibility
covers the explicit PTX spelling rcp.rn.f32: a reciprocal in binary32, the
standard 32-bit floating-point format, rounded to the
nearest representable result, resolving halfway cases toward an even final bit.
It preserves subnormal numbers, the small representable values near zero.
The target policy is the pinned PTX 9.4 version on sm_20 or later, where sm_20
denotes NVIDIA compute-capability level 2.0.
Other rounding modes, approximation, flushing small values to zero, and other
number formats are rejected rather than silently treated as this instruction.

links.reason: Normalization relies on the encoded nearest-even reciprocal with preserved subnormals and explicit target restrictions.

The input conditions are x<=m and abs(x),abs(m)<=2^124. These conservative bounds
prevent overflow in the negation, addition and base conversion. The proof derives
that the rounded difference is finite and nonpositive and hence reaches the
supported exponential domain. Finiteness or successful intermediate computations
are conclusions, not extra premises. Both signs of zero and gradual underflow
remain covered by the existing arithmetic contracts.
